newsitem.title: USA: Chicago's Cardinal Bernardin dead at age 68.
newsitem.headline: Chicago's Cardinal Bernardin dead at age 68.

text.p: Cardinal Joseph Bernardin, senior U.S. prelate in the Roman Catholic Church, died on Thursday after a 16-month battle with cancer, the Archdiocese of Chicago said.
Bernardin died at his residence at 1:33 a.m. local time (0733 GMT), Bob Quackenbush, a spokesman for the church, told Reuters.

Bernardin, the soft-spoken son of an Italian stone cutter, had talked by telephone in his final hours with both Pope John Paul II and President Bill Clinton. His death came a day before schoolchildren across the archdiocese were scheduled to assemble at special services to pray for him.

The pontiff called at mid-afternoon on Wednesday and "gave the cardinal his blessing. He thanked him for all that he had done for the Archdiocese of Chicago and for the universal church," a spokeswoman said on Wedneaday.

In June 1995 Bernardin was found to be suffering from pancreatic cancer, a particularly deadly form of the disease, and underwent surgery. Last Aug. 30 he announced the disease had spread to his liver and was inoperable, giving him less than a year to live.
A few weeks ago he abandoned chemotherapy treatments.
Throughout the process he had made his dying a public and spiritual event, preaching of it as a "transition from earth to life."

Bernardin, a native of Columbia, South Carolina, was the longest-serving active U.S. cardinal, appointed by Pope John Paul II in 1982 to head the 2.3 million-member Chicago archdiocese, the nation's second-largest after Los Angeles.
He had been a leader of the moderate to liberal wing of the church.
